skill.name: cursor
skill.description: Control the Cursor AI code editor from AI coding workflows with documented CLI actions for files, folders, diffs, extensions, and settings.
skill.summary: Open and manage Cursor editor sessions through documented CLI commands.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks in SKILL.md, not Ruby execution. The skill is a Cursor CLI reference with contextual risks around extension management and global Git configuration. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Extension commands can install third-party code into Cursor.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval and trusted extension identifiers before installing or uninstalling extensions.

remediation.issue: Global Git editor configuration changes persistent user settings.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before changing global Git settings, or prefer repository-scoped configuration when possible.

remediation.issue: SSH configuration paths can expose sensitive remote development metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Treat SSH configuration as sensitive and access it only when the user explicitly requests remote setup help.

content.user_title: Control Cursor from AI Coding Workflows
content.value_statement: Developers lose time when editor actions, file navigation, and diffs stay outside their AI coding workflow. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear Cursor CLI actions for files, folders, diffs, extensions, and remote setup.
actual_capabilities: Open files, folders, and projects in Cursor using CLI arguments.
Open files at specific lines and columns.
Start new windows or reuse existing Cursor windows.
Compare two files with Cursor diff mode.
List, install, uninstall, or disable Cursor extensions.
Show CLI help, version, verbose output, and developer tools.
limitations: Requires the Cursor CLI to be installed and available on PATH.
Does not provide Cursor authentication, licenses, or editor configuration.
Extension installation depends on valid extension identifiers and marketplace access.
Remote development still requires valid SSH setup outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Open Review Context
use_cases.description: Open the current project, a target file, or an exact line in Cursor during an assisted coding session.

use_cases.title: Compare Generated Changes
use_cases.description: Launch Cursor diff mode for two files so generated changes can be reviewed in the editor.

use_cases.title: Manage Editor Extensions
use_cases.description: List, install, uninstall, or disable Cursor extensions after confirming the requested editor change.

prompt_templates.title: Open Current Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for starting an editor session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open my current project in Cursor so I can inspect the files in the editor.

prompt_templates.title: Open File Location
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for jumping to a specific source location.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target file in Cursor at the line and column I provide, and reuse the current editor window.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review workflow for checking differences.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the two files I name in Cursor diff mode so I can review the changes side by side.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Editor Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow that combines project opening and extension review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this repository in Cursor, list installed extensions, and ask before installing or removing any extension.

output_examples.input: Open the current folder in Cursor.
output_examples.output: The assistant opens the active project in Cursor and reports whether the editor launch succeeded.

output_examples.input: Compare the generated file with the original file.
output_examples.output: The assistant opens a Cursor diff view so the two files can be reviewed side by side.

output_examples.input: Check which Cursor extensions are installed.
output_examples.output: The assistant requests the installed extension list and summarizes the extension identifiers returned by Cursor.

best_practices: Confirm target paths before opening or comparing files.
Ask before installing or uninstalling extensions.
Use diff mode for review before changing source files.
anti_patterns: Do not install extensions from untrusted publishers.
Do not point user data or extension directories at sensitive folders.
Do not inspect SSH configuration unless the user specifically asks.

faq.question: Does this skill run Cursor by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents Cursor CLI actions for an assistant to use when the user requests them.

faq.question: Can it install Cursor extensions?
faq.answer: Yes, it documents extension install and uninstall commands. Use explicit approval before changing editor extensions.

faq.question: Does it edit source files?
faq.answer: No direct editing logic is included. It opens files, folders, diffs, and editor tools through Cursor.

faq.question: Does it support remote development?
faq.answer: It notes Cursor remote workflows and the SSH config location. SSH setup and credentials remain outside the skill.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is Cursor required?
faq.answer: Yes. The Cursor CLI must be installed and available in the shell environment.
